# The Illusion of Productivity: Knowing When to Interrupt

A workshop can look productive because everybody is busy. Machines hum, hands move, conversations overlap, and the sheer volume of activity suggests that progress is being made. But busyness is not the same thing as progress. People may be working hard on entirely different problems, or worse, working on the wrong problem entirely. The person who pauses to ask a basic question can seem to slow things down, while actually preventing several days of wasted work. The challenge—and it is a genuine challenge, not a problem with a clean solution—is deciding when to interrupt and when to let an experiment finish.

## The Appearance of Work

Consider a software team in the middle of a sprint. Six developers are heads-down at their keyboards, typing steadily, committing code, closing tickets. From the outside, this is a picture of productivity.
